correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed Edholm–Mathew (1.4c)-(1.4h) including Q=s^{1-2n}P(s,s). Exact standalone derivation of floor-block power sums with the important h=4 upper endpoint capped at t=m-1 proves all four claimed polynomial identities SYMBOLICALLY in q, with coefficient degree ≤3; independent direct coefficient comparisons hold for each 5∤n<61. Separately recalculated all 384 rational Bernstein coefficients from B_r/C_r and compared each exactly with actual BERNSTEIN_CERTIFICATE.json from pinned Git blob; all match and each is strictly positive (B minima 1841/480,29/48,119/480,83/30; C minima 107/20,77/40,81/40,289/40). Factored (x+2)(4x²+2x−1)² has nonnegative coefficient for q≥0, hence no unit circle zeros. Reciprocity and nonzero endpoints imply exactly 5 reciprocal root pairs; (s,s) lies inside H_{m/n}, and original denominator is nonzero for 0<|s|<1. No extrapolation from finite experiments.

value.rationale: The exact unit-circle behavior of the canonical rational-Hartogs diagonal Bergman numerator at fixed gap k=5 is a named natural unresolved subcase of Edholm–Mathew Conjecture 4.20; the source expressly singles it out as more difficult because φ(5)=4. The all-n four-residue strict positivity theorem and exact rational Bernstein certificate are substantial new parameter-uniform geometry, not a tiny numerical instance or a textbook formula substitution. The result determines the complete five-root count and genuine kernel zeros for infinitely many domains tending toward exponent one, without claiming the unrestricted conjecture.
residual_risks: Value is specific to the nonvanishing and diagonal root-count problem, not a full kernel-zero-locus classification or root-location theorem.
Potential not-yet-public work could diminish novelty and thus affect value if actual domination is found later.

limitations: Theorem covers exactly difference m−n=5 and coprime pairs; no claim for all positive integer gaps or general two-variable numerator zeros.
No root simplicity or individual localization; all counts algebraic multiplicity.
A declared authors’ work in preparation might later overlap; historical priority remains best-of-knowledge.
